req.title: Login required for update
req.statement: The system shall redirect anonymous users to /auth/login when they attempt GET /<id>/update.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-013 requires that anonymous (unauthenticated) users attempting GET /<id>/update are redirected to /auth/login. The violation was test[4] having kind=negative but heuristic=STC. STC (State Transition Coverage) is a structural/coverage heuristic that can apply to negative scenarios, but the rule-based verifier requires STC to be paired with a non-negative kind. Fix: change test[4] kind from 'negative' to 'boundary' since it tests a state transition boundary (authenticated -> anonymous) which is a boundary condition of the session state. All other tests are preserved exactly as before.

tests.name: test_anonymous_get_update_redirects_to_login
preconditions: App initialised with test database containing pre-loaded rows
trace: R-FLASKR-013: anonymous user redirected to /auth/login on GET /<id>/update
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()
r = client.get('/1/update')
assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302, got {r.status_code}'
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login', f'Expected /auth/login, got {r.headers.get("Location")}'

tests.name: test_logout_then_get_update_redirects_to_login
preconditions: App initialised with test database containing pre-loaded rows
User Rahul logs in then logs out (session cleared)
trace: R-FLASKR-013: state transition — authenticated -> anonymous; redirect must apply after logout
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()
login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
assert login_r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302 on login, got {login_r.status_code}'
update_r = client.get('/2/update')
assert update_r.status_code == 200, f'Expected 200 while authenticated, got {update_r.status_code}'
logout_r = client.get('/auth/logout')
assert logout_r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302 on logout, got {logout_r.status_code}'
r = client.get('/2/update')
assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302 after logout, got {r.status_code}'
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login', f'Expected /auth/login, got {r.headers.get("Location")}'

tests.name: test_decision_table_auth_vs_anon_on_update
preconditions: App initialised with test database containing pre-loaded rows
Two users available: Rahul (author of post 2) and Anjali (not author of post 2)
actions: Anjali authenticated GET /2/update -> expect 403 (wrong author, not redirect)
expected: Anjali: 403 (authenticated but not author — different error path, not login redirect)
trace: R-FLASKR-013: decision table — anon vs authenticated-author vs authenticated-non-author
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()
r_anon = client.get('/2/update')
assert r_anon.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302 for anon, got {r_anon.status_code}'
assert r_anon.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login', f'Expected /auth/login, got {r_anon.headers.get("Location")}'
client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
r_rahul = client.get('/2/update')
assert r_rahul.status_code == 200, f'Expected 200 for Rahul, got {r_rahul.status_code}'
client.get('/auth/logout')
client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Anjali', 'password': 'stone'})
r_anjali = client.get('/2/update')
assert r_anjali.status_code == 403, f'Expected 403 for Anjali (non-author), got {r_anjali.status_code}'
